# The Great Advent Calendar Countdown

The seasonal treat-based countdown might these days have expanded into cosmetics and booze, but nothing beats 24 days of chocolate. For Emma Hartley, a devoted chocolate enthusiast and mother of three, the first of December always carried a particular kind of magic. She would rise before the children, make herself a strong cup of tea, and stand in the kitchen doorway simply admiring the three advent calendars lined up on the mantelpiece, their little numbered doors waiting patiently to be opened. It was, she had always believed, the purest form of anticipation that modern life could offer.

***

This year, however, something was different. Her eldest daughter, sixteen-year-old Sophie, had announced at the dinner table in late November that she considered herself too old for a chocolate advent calendar. She wanted the beauty version, the one filled with miniature lipsticks and tiny perfume samples that her friends were all talking about on social media. Emma had smiled diplomatically across the table, secretly feeling a small but significant piece of her heart quietly crumble away, like the corner of a particularly fine bar of dark chocolate.

***

Her youngest, seven-year-old Thomas, had no such complications. He had already identified his preferred calendar weeks in advance, a magnificent construction featuring his favourite cartoon characters behind each door, with milk chocolate shapes that bore absolutely no resemblance to anything festive but tasted, according to Thomas, like pure happiness. Each morning he would race downstairs in his dinosaur pyjamas, locate the correct number with tremendous concentration, and consume his chocolate with the solemn reverence of a tiny religious ceremony.

***

Her middle child, twelve-year-old Clara, sat somewhere philosophically between her siblings. She had accepted her traditional chocolate calendar with grace but had also begun casting curious glances at the beauty calendar sitting beside it on the mantelpiece. One morning Emma caught Clara carefully reading the ingredients list on the back of a miniature hand cream that had tumbled from Sophie's calendar, holding it up to the winter light coming through the frosted window with an expression of deep scientific interest.

***

By December the twenty-fourth, Emma reflected, standing in her kitchen with her morning tea growing cold, that perhaps the great expansion of the advent calendar into cosmetics and booze and candles and cheese and all manner of extraordinary things was not such a terrible development after all. It simply meant that the tradition had grown generous enough to accommodate everyone, at every stage of life. She reached up and opened her own calendar door, the one her husband had quietly purchased and placed on the counter without saying a word, and found inside a single perfect square of dark chocolate. It tasted, she decided, exactly like December.
